evals.prompt: Add type regression tests for a public generic helper.
evals.expected_behavior: Reads the nearest existing type test to match its tool and style (or inspects for an already-installed type-test tool if none exists), identifies the exact inference/assignability contract, and adds one positive and one negative case before broadening coverage.
assertions: Finds the nearest existing type-test convention or tool first before introducing a new one
Uses @ts-expect-error or an existing negative-assertion helper for the negative case
Adds one positive and one negative case rather than an exhaustive suite up front
Does not introduce new type-test tooling casually when an existing convention already fits

evals.prompt: Add exhaustive type tests covering every overload and argument permutation of this helper.
evals.expected_behavior: Keeps the test small and focused on the contract that actually needs protecting (public/exported surface, the motivating regression) rather than generating a giant fixture file enumerating every permutation, per the skill's preference for small focused assertions.
assertions: Prefers small, focused assertions over a giant fixture file enumerating every permutation
Focuses coverage on exported/intentionally shared types rather than every internal overload
Adds a regression case tied to the motivating bug rather than blanket exhaustive coverage

evals.prompt: Add a regression type test for the parseUser inference bug we just fixed.
evals.expected_behavior: Adds a positive case that encodes the correct inference and a negative case that fails for the right reason (via @ts-expect-error or an explicit non-assignability check), then runs the repository's type-test or typecheck command and confirms both cases behave as intended.
assertions: Negative case fails for the intended type reason, not from unrelated compiler noise
Runs the repository's existing type-test command or nearest equivalent typecheck fixture command after adding the test
Test stays about types (minimal runtime logic) rather than mixing in behavior assertions

evals.prompt: Add unit tests for runtime behavior only; no type inference contract changed.
evals.expected_behavior: Does not use the type-test workflow for ordinary runtime tests since no static type contract is being protected; routes to a runtime test skill instead.
assertions: Recognizes runtime tests are primary here, not a type contract
Does not add compile-time fixtures (@ts-expect-error, expectTypeOf) unnecessarily

evals.prompt: This bug only shows up when the function actually runs against malformed data at runtime, not in the type checker — write a test for it.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes this is a runtime-dependent contract (a documented red flag for this skill) and recommends a runtime test instead of forcing a compile-time type-test fixture.
assertions: Does not force a compile-time type-test fixture for a contract that only fails at runtime
Recommends a runtime test (optionally paired with a narrow typecheck fixture only for the static boundary)
